nodes.description: rWGS performance of all catalysts temperature screening 175-400°C
nodes.source_text: The catalytic testing was performed in a fixed-bed reactor with a feed gas of 24% CO2, 72% H2, and 4% Ar at atmospheric pressure. Figure 1a displays the catalytic performance of three Pd-FeO_x catalysts... the 5Pd-FeO_x catalyst exhibited... STY of 9.1 mmol_CO g_cat^-1 h^-1 at 250°C and 47.6 mmol_CO g_cat^-1 h^-1 at 400°C.

nodes.description: rWGS time-on-stream stability test at 400°C for 30h
nodes.source_text: time-on-stream (T-O-S) stability tests were carried out at 400°C under atmospheric pressure (Figure 1b). 5Pd-FeO_x showed the highest STY_CO (~46 mmol_CO g_cat^-1 h^-1) at the initial stage, which remains stable over the 30 h stability test with only slight deactivation (<3%).

nodes.description: rWGS time-on-stream stability test at 400°C for 30h
nodes.source_text: 0.05Pd-FeO_x shows a low STY_CO of ~26 mmol_CO g_cat^-1 h^-1 at the initial stage, but the activity of 0.05Pd-FeO_x gradually increases over the 30 h stability test, which eventually reaches ~41 mmol_CO g_cat^-1 h^-1.

For the 0.5Pd3Fe-FeO_x catalyst, the induction period was greatly shortened to less than ~5 h with an outstanding rWGS activity of ~40 mmol_CO g_cat^-1 h^-1... superior activity per Pd atom of 2.16 mmol_CO g_pd^-1 s^-1

nodes.characterization_summary: Fresh 5Pd-FeOx shows significantly large Pd particles of 4-5 nm; after 1h reaction shows Pd3Fe alloy formation with lattice spacing of 0.219 nm characteristic of (111) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fresh 5Pd-FeOx catalyst shows a significantly large Pd particle of 4-5 nm in size (Figure 1e and Figure S5). After the initial reaction, alloy formation on the 5Pd-FeOx catalyst was clearly observed, showing a typical lattice spacing of 0.219 nm, as characteristics of the (111) plane of the Pd3Fe alloy (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fresh 0.5Pd-FeOx shows homogeneous Pd nanoparticles of 1-2 nm; after 1h reaction shows thin FeOx overlayer encapsulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, the fresh 0.5Pd-FeOx catalyst showed homogeneous Pd nanoparticles with an average size of 1-2 nm (Figure 1g and Figure S8). After the reaction for 1 h at 400°C, a thin FeOx overlayer can be identified over the Pd NP.

nodes.characterization_summary: 0.05Pd-FeOx exhibits atomically dispersed Pd single-atom species on FeOx that remain stable without sintering after 1h reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 0.05Pd-FeOx catalyst exhibited an atomically dispersed Pd single-atom (SA) species on FeOx (Figure 1i and Figure S9) that remained stable without sintering after the reaction for 1h (Figure 1j).

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi in situ XPS Pd 3d of all three Pd-FeOx catalysts after reaction at 400°C for 1h: 5Pd-FeOx-1h Pd 3d5/2 at 335.5 eV (PdFe alloy), 0.5Pd-FeOx-1h at 335.2 eV (metallic Pd), 0.05Pd-FeOx-1h at 335.7 eV (Pdδ+).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quasi in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was further performed... As shown in Figure 1k, Pd the 3d5/2 binding energy (BE) of 5Pd FeOx-1h was located at 335.5 eV, as characteristic of the PdFe alloy. By contrast, the Pd 3d5/2 of 0.5Pd-FeOx-1h shifted to 335.2 eV, which is assigned to metallic Pd. A Pdδ+ state was observed on the 0.05Pd-FeOx-1h catalyst with a Pd 3d5/2 of 335.7 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: 5Pd-FeOx shows highest reducibility with lowest reduction temperature of Peak I; 0.5Pd-FeOx requires higher reduction temperature (>500°C) for Pd3Fe alloy formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The higher reducibility of 5Pd-FeOx as indicated by the lowest reduction temperature of Peak I, results in the enhanced FeOx reduction (Peak II) and thus the alloy formation (Peak III).

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi in situ XPS Fe 2p spectra show rapid carburization on 5Pd-FeOx after 1h at 400°C with FeCx at 707 eV; slower carburization on 0.05Pd-FeOx and 0.5Pd-FeOx over time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quasi in situ XPS experiments further reveal the dynamic carburization... After the reaction for 1h at 400°C, rapid carburization on the 5Pd-FeOx catalyst was immediately observed, as indicated by the emerging FeCx species at 707 eV in the Fe 2p XPS spectrum (Figure 2a).

nodes.evidence_snippet: After reaction, the 0.05Pd-FeOx spent catalyst exhibits the most prominent component of bulk Fe5C2 (48%), significantly higher than that of 0.5Pd-FeOx (39%) and 5Pd-FeOx (28%).

nodes.characterization_summary: 5Pd-FeOx-30h shows Fe5C2 encapsulation on Pd3Fe alloy NP (~5-6 nm) with characteristic Fe5C2 (510) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the 5Pd-FeOx-30h catalyst, the encapsulation of Fe5C2 was clearly observed on the outer surface of the Pd3Fe alloy NP (~5-6 nm, Figure S22), with a characteristic Fe5C2 (510) plane.
